videos.title: Inside Theranos with ex-Employee Tyler Shultz
videos.description:
With Theranos and Elizabeth Holmes back in the conversation, we’re revisiting one of the most remarkable firsthand accounts of what actually happened inside the company.

Tyler Shultz joined Theranos fresh out of Stanford as a true believer in its mission. His grandfather, former Secretary of State George Shultz, sat on the company’s board, and Elizabeth Holmes had become a mentor and even a presence at family gatherings. But once Tyler began working directly with Theranos’s technology, he discovered that the reality inside the lab looked very different from what the company was telling the world.

On The Social Radars, Tyler sat down with Jessica Livingston and Carolynn Levy to tell the full story of how he went from employee to whistleblower: the failed blood tests and red flags he uncovered, the culture of fear that kept employees silent, his attempts to raise concerns internally and with regulators, and the extraordinary legal pressure he faced after speaking to The Wall Street Journal.

This episode was originally recorded on December 4, 2024.

videos.title: Mike Volpi on Why AI Infrastructure Will Outlast the Hype Cycle
videos.description:
The internet boom built bandwidth. The AI boom is building intelligence. Mike Volpi, who helped shape Cisco’s strategy during the internet buildout, asks what that era can teach us about this one.

Mike joins a16z’s Raghu Raghuram and Guido Appenzeller to compare today’s investment in GPUs, data centers, and power with the fiber boom of the late 1990s, and explain why the infrastructure could prove valuable even if the market corrects.

They also discuss NVIDIA, custom silicon, networking, and the changing economics of GPUs, plus lessons from Cisco’s acquisition machine. And Mike explains why he thinks this technology cycle could be even more consequential than the last.

videos.title: Why FLUX 3 Trains on Images, Video and Sound — Andreas Blattmann & Dustin Podell, Black Forest Labs
videos.description:
A camera moves around a person. Halfway around, the model has to draw the back of a head it has never seen. How much can it learn about that missing view just by watching video? That’s the question we put to Andreas Blattmann and Dustin Podell of Black Forest Labs.

Their answer runs through FLUX 3. BFL trained one backbone on images, video and audio. The guests explain what each adds, how they decide which parts of denoising deserve the most compute, and why a detail that looks great in a still can flicker from frame to frame. We also get into the case for autoregression and where they think diffusion still has an edge.

There’s personal history here. Stable Diffusion is why Dustin left his software job and why swyx started Latent Space. They revisit the first FLUX training run in a French chalet, the photo experiment behind FLUX Kontext, and some of the things people actually use these models for, from restoring old family photos to generating a clip with synchronized sound.

videos.title: AI Realism Workflow the Pros Use (Eleven v4 + Seedance 2.5)
videos.description:
Keep your AI film characters sounding the same in every scene with Eleven v4 and Seedance 2.5.

Create AI Films → https://elevenlabs.io/creative?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=trend_tutorials&utm_content=create_consistent_character_voices_with_eleven_v4_and_seedance_2_5_ai_workflow

One of the biggest problems in AI filmmaking is characters losing their voice between scenes. In this workflow, we walk through how to pair Eleven v4 voice generation with Seedance 2.5 inside ElevenCreative so your character keeps the same voice, emotion, and delivery across every shot. We start by generating the perfect delivery in Eleven v4 using audio tags to direct the performance, then storyboard the scene in Flows with the voice over in place before generating any video.

From there we cover three ways to use that voice generation as a reference in Seedance 2.5, each one making the result more consistent:

• Method 1 • Use the Eleven v4 generation as an audio reference alongside a character reference and a set reference, then prompt the scene with tagged references
• Method 2 • Convert the MP3 into a plain black MP4 video and use it as a video reference, which tends to extract the delivery more reliably than the audio file
• Method 3 • Add a timestamp transcript from the black video using an LLM node, tag it in your prompt, and offset the timestamps so the action (like a crash landing) lands before the character starts speaking

We also cover choosing a voice from the Great voices for Eleven v4 selection in the voice library, lip syncing the generation to your character in Flows, and generating the scene separately so you can control the background. By the third method you can focus entirely on the prompt and the action while the voice delivery stays consistent every time.

videos.title: Turning Stranded Energy Into Intelligence: Crusoe CEO Chase Lochmiller
videos.description:
Chase Lochmiller runs one of the most operationally complex companies in AI: Crusoe builds power plants, manufactures electrical equipment, operates gigawatt-scale data centers, and runs a managed AI cloud on top, all under one roof. He just closed a round at a $31 billion valuation, and he got there by selling off the Bitcoin mining business that was paying the bills.

Chase explains why Crusoe is modeled on Exxon, not a cloud provider, and why he partners with companies that look like competitors. He makes the case that a company that outgrows the person who got it there is the rule, not the exception, and that CEOs almost always fire too slowly. He also talks candidly about hiring a coach, working hard to become a polished speaker when it didn’t come naturally, and why the data center industry’s biggest problem is a marketing problem.

I meet with a group of Sequoia founder CEOs between 20 and 2,000 employees, and one of them told me his business is becoming dizzyingly complex beneath him. Chase has the clearest answer I’ve heard for how to hold that in your head. 

And yes, we talk about summiting Everest.

videos.title: Inside the Robot Data Factory: Mecka's Josh Gao on Sensorizing Humans to Train Robots
videos.description:
Robotics never got the internet's gift of free training data, so someone has to manufacture it. Josh Gao, founder and CEO of Mecka AI, runs one of the largest robot data factories, and he explains what that actually involves: custom baseball caps and tactile gloves because nothing off the shelf captures force, 100-gigabit upload lines to move hundreds of petabytes, and custom quality gates. Josh lays out the training recipe the industry is converging on (roughly a million hours of egocentric human data, tens of thousands of hours of robot data, and a few hours of in-domain teleop ) and why tactile and simulation data still have to enter the "data pot of soup." He argues the field is still orders of magnitude behind Tesla's FSD, which spent a decade on two degrees of freedom while a robot hand has dozens. His take: there won't be a single GPT-3 moment for robotics, but a steady unlock of commercial tasks, starting with constrained industrial work and ending, he hopes, with robots mining asteroids.

Hosted by Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

videos.title: Why Own Your Intelligence? Harrison Chase Keynote | Interrupt London
videos.description:
Harrison Chase, Co-Founder and CEO of LangChain, explains what it means to own your intelligence, the specialization a team builds into the model, the harness, and the context, why he thinks agents need to be open, compounding, and governed to get there, and points to monday.com, Harvey, and Orange as examples of companies building the system around the model. He then walks through the LangSmith stack: Managed Deep Agents, which combines the Deep Agents harness and managed infrastructure into one, plus two agents LangChain built internally, Open SWE and its GTM Agent; observability on SmithDB, with Jev as a judge, RBAC on trace inputs and outputs, LangSmith Trajectories, the new AI Search, and LangSmith Custom Apps; and LangSmith Engine, where Engine v2 tests its own fixes on LangSmith Deployment and red teams your agent. He also introduces a self-report tool that agents can call to flag what went wrong while they run, and shares that Engine has scanned over 70 million traces and detected over 21,000 issues.

This session was captured at Interrupt London, the agent conference by LangChain.
